title: "Read" in the cave
hookLine: alone in the cave, he is seized by the angel Jibril, who says one word: read

cards: A night in Ramadan. He's in the cave, alone, as on so many nights. Suddenly, he isn't alone.
Someone is there, the angel Jibril, though he doesn't know that yet, and the angel says one word. Iqra. Read.
Recite. He answers honestly: I am not a reader. He had never learned to read or write.
The angel takes hold of him and squeezes him, hard, until he can't bear it, then lets go. Read. I am not a reader.

teach.h: THE FIRST WORDS TO COME DOWN.
teach.b: These are the first words of the Qur'an to come down, according to most Muslim scholars. They open Surah Al-'Alaq, the ninety-sixth.

In Pickthall's translation: “Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth, Createth man from a clot. Read: And it is thy Lord the Most Bountiful Who teacheth by the pen, Teacheth man that which he knew not.”
The first word of revelation is a command to read, given to a man who could not read.
Iqra comes from the root q-r-', to read, to recite aloud, and from that root comes the word Qur'an itself: the recitation. So the first word already names the whole book.

teach.h: IN THE NAME OF THY LORD.
teach.b: Then: in the name of your Lord. Not read anything, anyhow.

Read in the name; that's the bismillah from day one of this path, now as the very first instruction. Then who He is: the one who creates, who made the human being from a clinging clot, from almost nothing.
And then, twice, the pen: the one who teaches by the pen, who teaches the human being what he did not know.
A man who couldn't write is given, as his first revelation, a verse about writing and learning.
Muslims have taken that seriously for fourteen centuries: libraries, schools, the careful copying of the Qur'an by hand, the idea that seeking knowledge is part of faith.
The Qur'an says it came down in the month of Ramadan, on a night it calls Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Power, better than a thousand months.

how: Muslims remember the first revelation during Ramadan, especially in the last ten nights when many seek Laylat al-Qadr; many children learn Surah Al-'Alaq as one of their first surahs.

o: pray, the call heard from the minaret
read or recite, the first word revealed
write it down, the task of a scribe

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: the recitation, from the same root

s: the first word revealed of the Qur'an, most scholars say, was 'read'
Surah 96 opens: read: in the name of thy Lord Who createth.
the Prophet could read and write when the angel came
he answered, I am not a reader; Muslims describe him as unlettered.
the first revelation mentions the pen
who teacheth by the pen, teacheth man that which he knew not (96:4–5).

games.q: alone in the cave at night, he hears a command: read. he has never learned to read. what does he say?
games.why: he says honestly, I am not a reader, three times, before the angel recites the first verses to him (Bukhari).

practice: Take one line that matters to you, a verse, a poem, a sentence from a letter, or today's: read, in the name of thy Lord who createth.

Read it once at normal speed, then again far slower, one word at a time, letting each land before the next, and notice what you missed the first time. If you pray, you can begin with bismillah, as the first revelation did.

wordCard.voice: Iqra. Read, or recite: the first word of the Qur'an to be revealed, from the same root as the word Qur'an itself.

orig.note: Arabic: read, recite; from q-r-', the root of Qur'an.

carryVoice: Your line: read, in the name. Tomorrow, he runs down the mountain. Eighty-six days now.

sources.q: Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth, Createth man from a clot. Read: And it is thy Lord the Most Bountiful Who teacheth by the pen, Teacheth man that which he knew not.
